tasks.short: Establish and enforce rules for behavior and policies and procedures to maintain order among students.

steps.what: Establish rules, policies and procedures for behavior.
Read the posted behavior card before enforcing it.
Enforce those rules to maintain order among students.

tasks.design: The special education teacher establishes the behavior rules and posts the card in {DOCS}, then reads that card before enforcing the rules in the room. Enforcing stays with the teacher. Nothing sends a notice, raises an alert, or fills a sheet, and no tool watches the students.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rules lived in a long policy text, so finding the one that applies took a search.
tasks.enabler_now: A short card with the rule, who it covers and the consequence can be posted before the lesson.
tasks.still_hard: What just happened in the room is not on a card, and a tool must not watch the students to decide.
tasks.human_edge: Only the teacher sees what the student just did and chooses how to enforce the rule.
tasks.altitude: The week in the room does not change. Setting the rules and enforcing them stay with the teacher.

reach.task: Hear the behavior rule from the teacher before the lesson and apply it in the room.
reach.learn: A missing card is not a rule. They hear the rule from the teacher, not from a notice.

evidence.claim: Inferring pupils' emotions is prohibited. Enforcing stays in the room, and this design does not watch the students.
The rule that applies depends on what just happened in the room, which is not on the card.

assumptions: This task starts when the teacher sets or looks up the behavior rules for the students in front of them, and it ends when order is kept in the room. It does not include the student report or the individual plan.

The behavior card has three fields: rule, who it covers, and consequence. The special education teacher produces it in the establish step, and that posting time stays in that step. A blank consequence is not a rule.
If the card is missing, the read is not shorter: the teacher opens the policy text. The teaching assistant hears the rule from the teacher.
Nothing sends a notice, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. No tool watches the students. Existing document-store runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: What share of lessons already have a behavior card with the rule, who it covers, and the consequence filled in.
Whether the school already posts that card in the document store.
research_questions: What share of lessons have a behavior card with rule, coverage and consequence filled in?

already_counted.description: Setting the rules and posting the card stays inside the establish step.
Reading the card, including opening the policy text when the card is missing, stays inside the read.
Enforcing the rules in the room stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When the school renames a rule or a consequence, the teacher updates that field on the behavior card.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when no behavior card is posted, so the read is not shorter. High assumes the card is posted for about half the lessons, and setting and enforcing the rules stay at full time. The high end is not a figure from another school.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain accurate and complete student records, and prepare reports on children and activities, as required by laws, district policies, and administrative regulations.

steps.what: Read the posted card of this student's marks and notes.
Draft the report on children and activities from that card.

loop.input: The student, date, activity, mark and teacher note already on the card.
loop.output: Report sentences on the child and the activities.
loop.check: The special education teacher rejects any sentence whose claim is not on the card, and any sentence that adds a diagnostic label or a new mark.
loop.stop: One rejection and the special education teacher writes the report. The loop does not try again.
loop.why_not_simpler: The sentences are not a copy of the card fields.

steps.what: Prepare reports required by laws, district policies and administrative regulations.
Mark the record accurate and complete, or write it again.
Maintain student records by storing the accepted report.

tasks.design: The special education teacher reads the posted card in {DOCS}. A draft writes the report sentences from the marks and notes on that card only, the teacher accepts or rewrites those sentences and marks the record accurate and complete, and a write then stores that accepted report in {DOCS}. Nothing sends the report, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The report was composed by hand from notes scattered in the pupil file.
tasks.enabler_now: When the mark and the note are already fields on a card, a bounded draft can propose sentences and a file write can store the accepted report.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a narrative report draft is a high-risk system is unresolved. Many cards are free text. The teacher remains responsible for every sentence.
tasks.human_edge: Only the teacher knows whether a sentence is fair to this student and whether the record meets the regulation.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to composing sentences from fields already on the card. The teacher still decides what the report says and whether it is complete.

reach.task: Read the stored report in the pupil record when they need it.
reach.learn: The report is not sent. They open the stored record.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records, an OPP module and learning-goal tracking, and names no AI. This design stores the accepted report in the school's own record.
Rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026, and computers first scored 58% of 13,300+ raised reading scores. This design does not let a model assign or change a mark.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets the education level is high-risk. This draft does not set a level or a mark. Whether a narrative report draft still falls there is unresolved.
Inferring pupils' emotions is prohibited. This draft does not infer how a student feels.
WOR does not apply to schools. Under the WMS, staff consent to tools that can monitor them. This design does not monitor the teacher.
Support needs in a pupil plan are health data, and a new pupil-data system needs a DPIA. The teacher remains responsible for the report.

assumptions: This task starts when the teacher opens this student's record to prepare the required report, and it ends when the accepted report is stored or the teacher writes the report by hand. It does not include the lesson, the parent meeting, or sending the report.

The session card has five fields: student name, date, activity, mark, and teacher note. The special education teacher produces it at the end of the lesson. That posting time sits in the instruction task, which stays full time. A blank mark or a blank note is not a value. If any of the five fields is blank, the draft does not run and must not invent a sentence.

If the card is missing, the draft and the file write do not run, and the read is not shorter. The teacher writes the whole report. About half the cards may be free text, and on a free-text card those two steps do not run.

The draft runs inside the school's record environment and does not leave it. Whether a model host is outside the school is unknown, and the design forbids sending the text out. The draft does not assign a mark, set an education level, add a diagnostic label, or infer how the student feels.

The school does not file this report through a district portal. District in the task means the school's own rules and the regulations that apply to it. Nothing sends the report, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. Existing record runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: What share of student cards have student, date, activity, mark and note as separate fields.
Whether any report this teacher writes sets an education level.
Whether a model host would sit outside the school, and whether the school has completed a DPIA for a new pupil-data write.
What share of cards are free text.
research_questions: What share of student cards have student, date, activity, mark and note as separate fields, and does any report set an education level?

already_counted.description: Reading the card, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
Accepting or rewriting every report sentence stays inside the prepare step.
Marking the record complete, or writing it again, stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When a card column is renamed, the teacher checks that student, date, activity, mark and note still line up, and removes a stored sentence the new column would misstate.

approvals.approved_version: report sentences limited to the marks and notes on the card
the accepted report marked accurate and complete for this student and date

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the card is never posted, so the sentence step and the file write do not run and the teacher writes the whole report. High assumes about half the cards are free text, so those two steps do not run on that half. The high end is not a figure from a planning trial or from another school.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with parents, administrators, testing specialists, social workers, or other professionals to develop individual educational plans (IEPs) for students' educational, physical, and social development.

steps.what: Read the posted notes before this conference.
Confer with parents, administrators, testing specialists, social workers or other professionals.
Develop individual educational plans (IEPs) for students' educational, physical and social development.

tasks.design: The special education teacher reads the posted notes in {DOCS}, confers with the parent and the other professionals, and writes the individual educational plan after that meeting. Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet, and no model writes the plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes from parents and other professionals were long documents, and the plan had to be written in the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted note with source, date, concern and recommendation can be read before the meeting. A research project has said it will draft plan text, and it has published no results, so this design does not.
tasks.still_hard: The plan is a judgement made with the parent in the room. Which statute sets the deadline for a secondary school is unknown.
tasks.human_edge: The plan is set in the conversation with the parent and the other professionals. The teacher holds that conversation.
tasks.altitude: The meeting and the plan stay with the teacher. A posted note can shorten only the read before the meeting.

reach.task: Bring the concern and the recommendation to the meeting about the individual plan.
reach.learn: The plan is written by the teacher after the meeting.

evidence.claim: A NOLAI project will draft the OPP justification against quality criteria, and the page reports no results. This design does not draft the plan.

The cited act is the primary-education act, article 40a: an OPP is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and evaluated yearly. Whether that article binds this secondary school is unknown.
Under the WMS, parents and pupils consent to rules about pupil data. This design keeps the plan conversation with the parent and does not replace that consent.
Support needs can be health data. The plan is written by the teacher after the meeting.

assumptions: This task starts when the teacher prepares for the conference and ends when the teacher has written the individual educational plan. It does not include teaching the lesson or storing the activity report.

The note card has four fields: source role, date, concern, and recommendation text. The parent, the administrator, the testing specialist, or the social worker produces it in their own note. Their writing time is theirs. A blank recommendation is not a recommendation.

If the card is missing, the read is not shorter. No model writes the plan. No timer is started. The digest cites a primary-education act for a six-week deadline, and whether that article binds this secondary school is unknown.
Nothing sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. Existing document-store runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: Which statute, if any, sets the deadline for this secondary school's individual plan.
Whether notes from parents, the administrator, the testing specialist and the social worker already sit in the same record.
research_questions: Which statute, if any, sets the deadline for this secondary school's individual plan, and are the other professionals' notes already in the same record?

already_counted.description: Reading the posted notes, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
The conference with parents and the other professionals stays inside that step.
Writing the individual educational plan stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When a note-card column is renamed, the teacher checks that source role, date, concern and recommendation still line up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the note card is missing, so the read is not shorter. High assumes the note is posted for many but not all conferences, and the meeting and the plan stay at full time. The high end is under the three-point read saving and is not a measured figure from another school.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Employ special educational strategies and techniques during instruction to improve the development of sensory- and perceptual-motor skills, language, cognition, and memory.

steps.what: Read the posted strategy card before this lesson.
Employ special educational strategies and techniques during instruction to improve the development of sensory- and perceptual-motor skills, language, cognition, and memory.

tasks.design: The special education teacher reads the posted strategy card in {DOCS}, then employs the strategy during instruction. The lesson stays with the teacher. Nothing watches the lesson, infers emotion, sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The strategy sat inside a long plan, so finding it before the lesson took a search.
tasks.enabler_now: A card with the skill, the strategy and the technique can be posted from the plan.
tasks.still_hard: The lesson itself is judgement in the moment. A tool must not watch the student or infer emotion.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the student during the lesson and changes the technique in the moment.
tasks.altitude: The lesson stays with the teacher. A posted strategy card can shorten only the read before the lesson.

reach.task: Hear which perceptual-motor strategy the lesson used.
reach.learn: They hear it from the teacher, not from a notice. The strategy card is not their own lesson plan.

evidence.claim: Inferring pupils' emotions is prohibited. This design does not infer how a student feels.
AI that watches tests is high-risk. This design does not watch the lesson or score it.
Which strategy to use depends on the student in front of the teacher.

assumptions: This task starts when the teacher looks up the strategy for this lesson and ends when the lesson is given. It does not include writing the plan or the activity report.

The strategy card has four fields: student, skill (sensory, perceptual-motor, language, cognition, or memory), strategy, and technique. The special education teacher produces it when they write the individual plan, and that writing stays full time on the plan task. A blank strategy is not a strategy.
If the card is missing, the read is not shorter. Nothing watches the lesson, infers emotion, sends a record, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. Existing document-store runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: What share of strategy cards name the student, the skill, the strategy and the technique.
Whether any student's support needs are stored as health data on that card.
research_questions: What share of strategy cards name the skill, the strategy and the technique, and are any students' support needs stored as health data in that card?

already_counted.description: Reading the strategy card, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
Employing the strategy during instruction stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When a strategy-card column is renamed, the teacher checks that student, skill, strategy and technique still line up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the strategy card is missing, so the read is not shorter. High assumes the card is posted for many but not all lessons, and the instruction stays at full time. The high end is under the three-point read saving and is not a measured figure from another school.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the lesson, the rules in the room, and the meeting about the plan. Less of it is searching for a posted note. Report sentences come from marks and notes already on the card, and the teacher still accepts every report before it is stored.
reach: Behavior rules are posted by the special education teacher before the lesson that uses them, and the teacher still enforces them.
Marks and notes are on the card before a report is written, and the teacher still accepts the report and marks it complete.
Parents, the administrator, the testing specialist and the social worker still meet to set the individual plan, and a model does not write that plan.
skills_to_grow: Reject a report sentence the mark or the note does not support
Refuse a model that writes the individual educational plan or sets a mark
Refuse a tool that watches a lesson or infers how a student feels
role.ambitious_version: The cards are already posted. The teacher still sets the rules, teaches the lesson, holds the meeting, and signs the report.
